## Step 1: Develop initial scraper and crawler
```{python}
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import pandas as pd
from urllib.parse import urljoin

URL = "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"

resp = requests.get(URL, timeout=30)
resp.raise_for_status()

soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "html.parser")

rows = []

category_selectors = ["h2", "h3"]
current_category = None
root = soup.find("main") or soup

for tag in root.find_all(category_selectors + ["a"], recursive=True):
    if tag.name in category_selectors:
        text = tag.get_text(strip=True)
        if text:
            current_category = text
        continue

    if tag.name == "a":
        title = tag.get_text(" ", strip=True)
        href = tag.get("href")

        if not title or not href:
            continue

        full_link = urljoin(URL, href)

        if "/fraud/enforcement/" not in full_link:
            continue
        if full_link.rstrip("/") == URL.rstrip("/"):
            continue

        container = tag.find_parent(["li", "div", "article", "section"]) or tag.parent

        date = None
        time_tag = container.find("time")
        if time_tag and time_tag.get_text(strip=True):
            date = time_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        else:

            candidates = container.find_all(["span", "p", "div"], limit=6)
            for c in candidates:
                t = c.get_text(" ", strip=True)
                if any(m in t for m in ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
                                        "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]) or \
                   any(ch.isdigit() for ch in t) and len(t) <= 30:
                    date = t
                    break

        rows.append({
            "title": title,
            "date": date,
            "category": current_category,
            "link": full_link
        })

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)

df = (
    df.dropna(subset=["title", "link"])
      .drop_duplicates(subset=["title", "link"])
      .reset_index(drop=True)
)

print(df.head())
```

## Step 2: Making the scraper dynamic

### 1. Turning the scraper into a function 

* a. Pseudo-Code

Inputs: start_year, start_month, run_scraper (bool)

Guardrail: If start_year < 2013: print “restrict to >= 2013” and return None.

Set start date cutoff: start_date = datetime(start_year, start_month, 1)

Initialize: page = 1, rows = [ ], keep_going = True

while loop:

    * Build URL:

        if page == 1: base URL

        else: base URL + ?page=page

    * Request page HTML

    * Parse all enforcement “items” on the page

    * If no items found → break (end of pagination)

    * For each item:

        Extract title, date, link

        Track the current category heading (e.g., most recent < h2 >/< h3 >)

        Convert date string → datetime

        If date < start_date: set keep_going = False

        Else: append row to rows

    * page += 1

    * sleep(1) to be polite

    * if keep_going == False: break

Make tidy dataframe with columns: title, date, category, link

Sort by date (optional), save to CSV: enforcement_actions_< year >_< month >.csv

Return dataframe

We are using a while loopb because we don’t know how many pages you need ahead of time. It iwill stop when it hits an old enough date or there’s no next page.

* b. Create Dynamic Scraper

```{python}
import time
import re
from datetime import datetime
from urllib.parse import urljoin

import requests
import pandas as pd
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser as dateparser  # pip install python-dateutil (often already installed)


BASE_URL = "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"


def scrape_enforcement_actions_since(start_year: int,
                                     start_month: int,
                                     run_scraper: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    """
    Scrape HHS OIG enforcement actions from (start_year, start_month) through today.
    Saves to: enforcement_actions_<year>_<month>.csv
    If run_scraper is False, does nothing (so knitting is fast).
    """

    if not run_scraper:
        print("run_scraper=False, skipping scrape (use saved CSV instead).")
        return None

    if start_year < 2013:
        print("Year must be >= 2013 (HHS OIG enforcement actions only listed after 2013).")
        return None

    if start_month < 1 or start_month > 12:
        raise ValueError("start_month must be between 1 and 12.")

    start_date = datetime(start_year, start_month, 1)

    session = requests.Session()
    session.headers.update({
        "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; course scraper; +https://oig.hhs.gov/)"
    })

    rows = []
    page = 1
    keep_going = True

    while keep_going:
        url = BASE_URL if page == 1 else f"{BASE_URL}?page={page}"
        r = session.get(url, timeout=30)
        r.raise_for_status()

        soup = BeautifulSoup(r.text, "html.parser")
        main = soup.find("main") or soup

        # Strategy:
        # - Walk through headings (h2/h3) to capture category
        # - Collect links to individual enforcement action pages
        current_category = None
        items_found_on_page = 0

        # We scan in document order to "carry" the category heading down
        for node in main.find_all(["h2", "h3", "a"], recursive=True):

            if node.name in ["h2", "h3"]:
                txt = node.get_text(" ", strip=True)
                if txt:
                    current_category = txt
                continue

            if node.name == "a":
                title = node.get_text(" ", strip=True)
                href = node.get("href")
                if not title or not href:
                    continue

                full_link = urljoin(BASE_URL, href)

                # Keep only links that look like individual enforcement entries
                # (This filter is important to avoid grabbing nav/footer links.)
                if "/fraud/enforcement/" not in full_link:
                    continue
                if full_link.rstrip("/") == BASE_URL.rstrip("/"):
                    continue

                container = node.find_parent(["li", "article", "div", "section"]) or node.parent

                # Try to extract date: prefer <time>, fallback to nearby text
                date_text = None
                time_tag = container.find("time")
                if time_tag:
                    date_text = time_tag.get("datetime") or time_tag.get_text(" ", strip=True)

                if not date_text:
                    # fallback: search nearby text for a date-like string
                    nearby = container.get_text(" ", strip=True)
                    # crude pattern, but works as a fallback:
                    # e.g., "January 12, 2024"
                    m = re.search(r"(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\s+\d{1,2},\s+\d{4}", nearby)
                    if m:
                        date_text = m.group(0)

                if not date_text:
                    # If date is missing, skip (or keep with None if you prefer)
                    continue

                try:
                    dt = dateparser.parse(date_text).replace(tzinfo=None)
                except Exception:
                    continue

                items_found_on_page += 1

                # Stop condition: once we hit older than start_date, we can stop after this page scan
                if dt < start_date:
                    keep_going = False
                    continue

                rows.append({
                    "title": title,
                    "date": dt.date().isoformat(),   # tidy ISO date
                    "category": current_category,
                    "link": full_link
                })

        if items_found_on_page == 0:
            # no enforcement items recognized => likely end of pagination or selector mismatch
            break

        page += 1
        time.sleep(1)

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).drop_duplicates(subset=["title", "link"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Sort so "earliest scraped" is easy to find
    if not df.empty:
        df = df.sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

    outname = f"enforcement_actions_{start_year}_{start_month:02d}.csv"
    df.to_csv(outname, index=False)
    print(f"Saved {len(df)} rows to {outname}")

    return df
```

## Step 3: Plot data based on scraped data

### 1. Plot the number of enforcement actions over time

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

df = pd.read_csv("/Users/Swaggy-LYX/Downloads/enforcement_actions_2022_01.csv")

df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])

df.head()
```

```{python}
df["year_month"] = df["date"].dt.to_period("M").dt.to_timestamp()

monthly_counts = (
    df
    .groupby("year_month")
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)
```

```{python}
alt.Chart(monthly_counts).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month"),
    y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Enforcement Actions"),
    tooltip=["year_month:T", "n_actions:Q"]
).properties(
    title="HHS OIG Enforcement Actions Over Time (Since Jan 2022)",
    width=650,
    height=350
)
```


### 2. Plot the number of enforcement actions categorized:

* based on "Criminal and Civil Actions" vs. "State Enforcement Agencies"
```{python}
def classify_category_from_title(title: str) -> str:
    t = str(title).lower()
    state_markers = [
        "attorney general", "ag ", "medicaid fraud control unit", "mfcu",
        "state", "commonwealth", "department of justice", "doj",
        "office of inspector general", "state of", "kentucky", "ohio", "texas",
        "florida", "new york", "california"  # optional: remove if too aggressive
    ]
    if any(k in t for k in state_markers):
        return "State Enforcement Agencies"
    return "Criminal and Civil Actions"

df["category_fixed"] = df["title"].apply(classify_category_from_title)
df["category_fixed"].value_counts()

```

```{python}
monthly_by_category = (
    df.groupby(["year_month", "category_fixed"])
      .size()
      .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)

```

```{python}
alt.Chart(monthly_by_category).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month"),
    y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Actions"),
    color=alt.Color("category:N", title="Category"),
    tooltip=["year_month:T", "category:N", "n_actions:Q"]
).properties(
    title="Enforcement Actions by Category",
    width=650,
    height=350
)

```

* based on five topics

```{python}
cca = df[df["category_fixed"] == "Criminal and Civil Actions"].copy()
```

```{python}
def classify_topic(title):
    title = title.lower()
    
    if any(word in title for word in ["health", "medicare", "medicaid", "hospital", "physician", "clinic"]):
        return "Health Care Fraud"
    elif any(word in title for word in ["bank", "financial", "loan", "wire", "securities", "money laundering"]):
        return "Financial Fraud"
    elif any(word in title for word in ["drug", "opioid", "pharmacy", "controlled substance"]):
        return "Drug Enforcement"
    elif any(word in title for word in ["bribe", "corrupt", "kickback"]):
        return "Bribery/Corruption"
    else:
        return "Other"

cca["topic"] = cca["title"].apply(classify_topic)

cca["topic"].value_counts()

monthly_by_topic = (
    cca
    .groupby(["year_month", "topic"])
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)

```

```{python}
alt.Chart(monthly_by_topic).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month"),
    y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Actions"),
    color=alt.Color("topic:N", title="Topic"),
    tooltip=["year_month:T", "topic:N", "n_actions:Q"]
).properties(
    title="Criminal and Civil Enforcement Actions by Topic",
    width=650,
    height=350
)

```
